correct_completion: I will have completed my degree.
full_sentence: By next June, I will have completed my degree.
acceptable_variants: I will have finished my degree.
my degree will have been completed.

options.text: I completed my degree last June.
options.why_wrong: The past simple describes a completed event in the past. The sentence needs a future time and a future completion point, so this option uses the wrong tense.
The present continuous describes an action in progress now. It does not show an action that will already be finished by a future time.

options.text: I will have completed my degree.
I will be completing my degree.
options.why_wrong: The future continuous describes an action that will be in progress at a future time. The sentence needs an action that will already be finished by then.

grammar_focus: Future perfect with 'by' and a future time expression
explanation: The phrase 'by next June' sets a deadline in the future. The future perfect, formed with will have plus the past participle, shows that the action will be finished before that deadline. Turkish speakers may use a simple future tense here because Turkish marks this meaning with a separate verb suffix, so the English perfect form needs deliberate practice.
translation: Gelecek Haziran'a kadar lisans eğitimimi tamamlamış olacağım.
